You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Meta Q2 Earnings Preview: AI Spending Guidance and Ad Monetization in Focus

TEXT:
1. Investment Highlights at a Glance
Meta will report its second-quarter 2026 results after the U.S. market close on July 29 (early morning Beijing time on July 30). Consensus expects revenue of approximately $60.258 billion (+7.01% QoQ) and EPS of $7.23 (-30.79% QoQ). Following Alphabet ’s recent drop of 6.89% after AI-related capital expenditures doubled year-over-year and free cash flow turned negative for the first time, investors are closely watching Meta—another heavy AI spender—for clarity on whether its advertising business can continue delivering AI-driven efficiency gains and whether full-year capital expenditure guidance will be raised again.
2. Four Key Focus Areas
Focus 1: AI-Driven Conversion Performance in Advertising
Advertising remains Meta’s dominant cash-flow engine. First-quarter 2026 ad revenue reached $55.024 billion , accounting for 97.7% of total revenue. Both Bank of America and Deutsche Bank are constructive: BofA raised its Q2 revenue estimate to $60.6 billion and EPS to $7.5 , citing strong ad demand plus AI efficiency gains that could push results above consensus. Deutsche Bank described channel checks as “overwhelmingly positive,” with advertisers seeing higher conversion rates and improved return on ad spend thanks to AI-powered ranking, retrieval, and automation. Advantage+ is now used by 82% of Meta advertisers, and the value-optimization suite has reached an annualized revenue run-rate of more than $20 billion (more than double the level a year earlier). Clear outperformance in ad growth and AI contribution would provide direct support for the valuation.
Focus 2: Whether Capex Guidance Will Be Raised Again
In April, Meta raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $125–145 billion , nearly double the $72.2 billion spent in 2025, primarily for GPUs, data centers, and AI infrastructure. Bank of America notes that higher memory and chip costs could prompt management to lift the range further to $135–150 billion . Markets remain concerned that elevated spending will continue to pressure near-term profits and free cash flow; the latest guidance delivered on the earnings call will be a key catalyst or pressure point for the stock.
Focus 3: Path to Monetizing AI Compute Externally
On July 1, reports that Meta is planning to sell AI compute capacity and model access to external customers—potentially via two models: hosted full-model access (comparable to AWS Bedrock) or raw GPU rental (comparable to CoreWeave )—sent the stock up 8.81% . Deutsche Bank’s base case assumes Meta will add 5 GW of compute capacity in 2026, reaching 7 GW by year-end, and plans to rent out 15–20% of idle capacity while prioritizing internal needs for ad recommendation, the Muse model, and AI agents. This initiative is viewed as a critical step in converting AI infrastructure from a pure cost center into a revenue-generating asset. Near-term progress and management commentary will determine whether the market buys the story.
Focus 4: Implications of the Revenue–EPS Divergence
Consensus shows revenue rising quarter-over-quarter while EPS is expected to decline sharply. This divergence clearly reflects institutional concern that heavy AI spending is eroding profitability. Results that deliver both strong ad growth and controlled capital spending would help ease the valuation pressure created by this gap; the opposite outcome could trigger an Alphabet-style sell-off.
3. Risks and Opportunities Coexist
Upside Catalysts:
Advertising revenue and AI-tool contribution clearly exceed expectations, with Advantage+ and related products continuing to lift conversion rates and ARPU.
Capital expenditure guidance remains unchanged or is raised only modestly, accompanied by a clear timeline and scale for external compute monetization.
Management emphasizes that AI is already delivering measurable returns in advertising and user experience, reinforcing the narrative that the spending is justified.
Downside Risks:
Full-year capital expenditure guidance is raised substantially into the zone that concerns investors, further pressuring free cash flow.
Ad growth falls short of expectations or AI conversion benefits fail to materialize fully, reinforcing the “spend without return” narrative.
Options implied volatility is already elevated (IV 51.87% , 96th percentile); a muted reaction to results could trigger rapid IV crush and heightened stock volatility.
4. Trading Strategy Considerations
Bull Case: Stronger-than-expected advertising results, clear guidance on AI monetization, and contained capital spending could allow the market to re-rate Meta’s AI investment cycle, supporting a recovery from recent spending-related discounts.
Bear Case: A significant upward revision to capital expenditure guidance or weaker-than-expected AI-driven ad performance could trigger an Alphabet-style after-hours decline and amplify downside pressure in a high-volatility options environment.
Key Metrics to Watch:
Ad revenue growth rate and contribution from AI tools
Latest full-year capital expenditure guidance
Progress and scale of external compute rental
Free cash flow and margin trends
Operational Suggestions: Prefer a wait-and-see or lightly hedged stance ahead of the report. Traders expecting elevated volatility but uncertain direction may consider long straddle or strangle structures. Shareholders seeking to hold through the event can use a collar (long put + short call) to limit downside. Short-term traders should focus on after-hours guidance and conference-call remarks regarding the AI return timeline; longer-term investors should continue to anchor on advertising fundamentals and tangible monetization evidence.
